title: Tabbouleh Chicken Bowls
shortDescription: Herb-heavy bulgur salad topped with lemon grilled chicken
subtitle: Herb-heavy bulgur salad topped with lemon grilled chicken
description: Fine bulgur tabbouleh with parsley, mint, tomato, and cucumber tops with grilled lemon chicken for a bright, herb-forward bowl line.

steps.title: Gather ingredients and equipment
steps.instruction: Line up every ingredient for Tabbouleh Chicken Bowls in the order you will cook — measure spices into ramekins, trim proteins on a dedicated board, and set tongs, thermometers, and hotel pans within arm's reach before any heat goes on.

steps.title: Preheat ovens and surfaces
steps.instruction: Preheat ovens, griddles, or grills to recipe temp before the crew arrives — cold equipment extends cook time and dries out batch chicken. Confirm burners ignite evenly and sheet pans are greased or lined.

steps.title: Soak bulgur
steps.instruction: Cover bulgur with boiling water, cover bowl, soak 15–20 minutes until tender and fluffy. Drain thoroughly and fluff with a fork. Maintain a steady simmer — bubbles should break the surface without a rolling boil that shreds delicate proteins. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Build tabbouleh
steps.instruction: Toss bulgur with parsley, mint, tomato, cucumber, half the lemon juice, olive oil, garlic, and salt until herbs evenly distributed. Plan about 15 minutes for this step at crew scale. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Season and cook chicken
steps.instruction: Rub chicken with remaining lemon juice, salt, and pepper. Grill or roast 16–18 minutes until 165°F with light char marks on exterior. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Rest and slice
steps.instruction: Rest chicken 5 minutes, slice thin. Meat should be white throughout with juices running clear, not pink at the center. Hold covered at 140°F up to 20 minutes — log the time if your hall tracks food safety during long shifts. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Verify safe internal temps
steps.instruction: Spot-check the thickest pieces with an instant-read thermometer — target 165°F. If any piece reads low, return it to heat immediately rather than holding under temp on the line.

steps.title: Assemble bowls
steps.instruction: Portion tabbouleh into bowls, top with sliced chicken and green onions. Salad should taste bright and herb-forward, not oily. Plan about 5 minutes for this step at crew scale. Keep a backup tray at 200°F for firefighters returning from a call — never serve picked-over pans to late crew. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

proTips: More parsley than bulgur is traditional—do not skimp on herbs.
Prep tabbouleh 2 hours ahead so flavors meld; add chicken at service.
Feta crumble adds salt if crew finds tabbouleh too lean.
tonightSpread: Baba ganoush if available from store.
leftovers: Tabbouleh keeps 2 days; add fresh chicken when serving.
Wrap in pita with hummus spread.
whyCrewsLikeIt: Reset meal after heavy comfort-food weeks. Huge flavor from herbs without heavy sauces.
mealPrepNotes: Soak bulgur while prepping herbs. Chop herbs coarse—not puréed—for authentic texture. Station: Drain bulgur well or bowls turn watery at the line. Station: Grill chicken on flat-top or roast on sheet pan depending on equipment. Station: Bowl line: tabbouleh base, sliced chicken, extra lemon, feta optional.
